name: Aqua Adventures
summary: Aqua Adventures runs whale watching and whale swim trips, island eco cruises, snorkel tours and guided dives from its centre at 95 Marine Parade, Southport on the Gold Coast. Whale trips run in the humpback season on small boats, and the dive and snorkel trips go to Wave Break Island, the Scottish Prince wreck and offshore reefs. The business was formed by combining several long-running Gold Coast ocean companies.
standouts: Describes itself as a PADI 5 Star Instructor Development Centre, in business for more than 30 years under its earlier name Surfers Paradise Divers
Small boat whale tours with optional whale research activities for guests
Names Humpbacks and High-rises, Dolphin Research Australia and Sea Shepherd as research projects it supports
Stand-by ticket offered if no whales are spotted on a designated whale watch tour between June and September

trips.title: Boutique Whale Watching Tour
trips.summary: A two to three hour whale watching cruise from Southport on the Gold Coast, run as a small group with a stated limit of 12 passengers. The crew look for humpback whales in the open ocean beyond the Broadwater, and guests can take part in simple whale research tasks if they want to. Tours leave on selected days in the morning or around midday.
highlights: Small group, with a stated maximum of 12 passengers
Up to two departures a day on selected days, including a morning and a midday tour
Optional whale research activities, using survey sheets and a hydrophone
Stand-by ticket offered if no whales are spotted on a designated tour between June and September
trips.duration: 2.5 hours (approx.), minimum 2 hours and up to 3 hours if whales are not found early
trips.departsFrom: Aqua Adventures Centre, 95 Marine Parade, Southport
includes: Optional whale research activities (survey data sheets and a hydrophone to listen to underwater sounds)
bring: Seasickness medication if needed, taken well before departure
trips.requirements: Moderate fitness and mobility are needed to board, get off and hold on while the boat is moving. Anyone with a serious medical condition, including pregnancy or a physical disability, should email the operator or check with their doctor before booking. Children under 2 are free and sit on a parent's lap.
trips.checkNotes: No current price is shown on the page. The only prices are a '2023 Early Bird Price' of $65 per person (limited time offer) and a private charter for up to 42 people at $2200; both were left out as out of date or tied to a larger boat. Prices and dates sit inside an embedded Rezdy calendar widget (aquaadventures.rezdy.com, calendarWidget 715697, not opened), so the page URL is recorded as the booking link. The page contradicts itself about the boat: the intro says an 8.5m RIB called Big Blue 1 with 12 passengers, while the highlights and vessel text name Game Changer, a 12m catamaran for up to 42 guests. The booking steps also say tours need at least 10 participants to depart. Minimum age is stated differently across the site (12 on the whale watching page, 5 for whale watching on the Aqua Cruise page, and 'children of all ages' in another answer). Season is June to November in the FAQ, June to October in the intro text, and the sighting guarantee covers June to September only. Departure times are as stated (meet 08:30 for 09:00, meet 11:30 for 12:00) but the page says they vary with tides and are on selected days. The title is copied from the page text; the whale watching hub card calls it 'Small Boat Whale Watching Tours'.

highlights: Swim beside humpback whales when they come close to the boat
Observers can join on the larger boat without swimming
Minimum age 10 for swimmers
Whale swim is offered from August to October on private charters

The menu-style link /whale-watching-gold-coast/swim-with-whales-gold-coast/ redirects to the Aria Cruises sailing catamaran page, and /whale-tours-whale-watching/ redirects back to the whale watching hub. The hub lists 'Swim With Whales Tours' with 'Enquire Now' buttons and the Aqua Cruise page describes the swim, so it is treated as enquiry only. The only price is the $180 per person add-on on the private charter page; that charter page has a Rezdy calendar widget (599484) with an optional 'Add any Whale Swimmers' step, so a swim may be bookable through the charter. Options include a private whale watching trip from June to October, a whale swim for the group from August to October, a Broadwater cruise with an island stopover, or a private scuba or snorkelling outing. Charters run any day of the week with a qualified skipper.

trips.title: South Stradbroke Island Eco Cruise
trips.summary: A two to three hour cruise from Southport through the Gold Coast Broadwater, with a stopover at South Stradbroke Island at Tipplers Cafe or Couran Cove. Dolphins, turtles, rays and dugongs may be seen along the way, and shore birds along the island foreshore. Food and drink on the island are at your own cost.

trips.title: Scottish Prince Wreck Dive
trips.summary: A dive on the Scottish Prince, a 64 m iron barque that lies about 800 m off the Southport Spit. The hull is covered in soft corals and sponges, and crayfish, shovelnose rays, brown-banded cat sharks and wobbegong sharks are seen there. The wreck is protected under the Commonwealth Historic Shipwreck Act, so divers are asked to take nothing from it.

checkNotes: Scope: this is a multi-brand Gold Coast business (Aqua Dive, Aqua Cruise, Aqua Hire, Aqua Fish, Aqua Marina) that took over older businesses, including Sea the Gold Coast, Surfers Paradise Divers and Mac's Boat Hire. Twelve trips with their own pages were captured; the brief's whale swim and dolphin eco cruise are the first five. Whale pages are out of date and contradict each other: they mix 2023, 2025 and 2026 seasons; three boats (Salty Kiss 7.66m for 10 guests, Big Blue 1 at 8m or 8.5m for 12 guests, and Game Changer at 11.99m, 12m or 40 foot for up to 42 guests); three minimum ages (12, 10 and 5); and a 2023 early bird price. Confirm current boats, prices, ages and times with the operator before publishing. Whale swim licence: the site does not say which permit the operator holds. Queensland allows swimming with whales only for licensed operators. Not captured as trips: (1) Whale watching on a sailing catamaran with partner Aria Cruises (page /whale-watching-gold-coast/whale-watching-sailboat-cruise/): $119 per person, 4 hours, 9:00 am session, 28 passengers, June to September; the page says bookings are managed by Aria Cruises, a different business, through a FareHarbor link (fareharbor.com/embeds/book/sailmoretonbay/, not opened), so it was not listed as this operator's trip. (2) Motorised Watersports: appears only as a menu and tile link into a Rezdy catalogue (aquaadventures.rezdy.com/catalog/627098/motorised-watersports, not opened) with no page. (3) Self-drive boat hire, kayak hire and stand-up paddle board hire (hire page lists 4 person and 6 to 8 person boats): these are rentals, not tours, the hire page shows half day $299 and full day $499 in one place and half day $150 and full day $180 in its FAQ, and its booking widget is a FareHarbor link to 'capriboathire', so they were left out. (4) Guided Kayak Tours: page says 'Coming Soon'. (5) Fishing charters: the page says 'Coming soon', and the inshore charter text has no price. (6) PADI courses: about thirty course pages exist under /scuba-diving-gold-coast/; only two were read. The 'Open Water Diver Course' page is written for independent PADI instructors (from $395, product code IIOWD), and the offers page's 'Book Here' button for the $695 Open Water offer redirects to the PADI Scuba Diver Course page (from $385, 2 days, minimum age 10, product code SD). Courses were not listed as trips; a person should decide whether to add them. Dive internship, dive club and Bubblemaker parties were not read. (7) 'Dolphin & Marine Life Cruises' and '3 Day Humpback Whale Research and Rescue Expeditions' appear in lists on the hub and Aqua Cruise page with no page of their own. Contact: the site shows two emails. The footer shows info@aquaadventurecentre.com.au as text but the link behind it goes to a different personal address, and a second line shows info@aquaadventures.com.au (used here). Phone is 07 5591 7117; the Aqua Cruise page shows (07) 2102 4365 for charters. Opening hours shown are Monday to Sunday 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. Prices are 'from' prices shown on product pages; passenger types and full price lists sit inside Rezdy widgets that were not opened. The site's FAQ page contains only placeholder text. Google review text on the homepage was not used. Pages read: about 34, one at a time with plain curl and WebFetch; no bot check, captcha or block was met. Several links redirected to the hub page (/whale-watching-gold-coast/gold-coast-whale-watching/, /whale-tours-whale-watching/, /gold-coast-whale-adventures/).
